card.name: Interacting drug named before its effect
card.fires_on: The last word of a drug name, or the linking word right after it (to, may), in interaction text where the drug is about to be said to change another drug's effect or be combined with it.

modes.label: Drug name in co-use
modes.description: End of a drug name in a phrase about using it together with another drug.
modes.example: The concurrent use of aspir<<in>> and an NSAID, such as nap

modes.label: Linking word before an effect
modes.description: A word like may or to after a drug name, leading into a stated change in another drug's effect.
modes.example: neuroleptics (e.g., phenothiazines, butyrophenones, thioxanthenes) or metoclopramide<< may>> reduce the efficacy of ropinirole extended

card.writes: It seems to push toward words that continue a phrase about a drug acting alongside another, and away from words meaning "itself" or "alone".
card.plain: It lights up in drug-interaction sentences at the point where a drug has been named and the text turns to what it does with another drug.
